title: Hemispheric routing safeguard with graded shedding and escape hysteresis
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design and implement a hemispheric-level routing safeguard that enforces SLO-driven steering, capacity-aware soft-pinning, and graded load-shedding. The feature is intended to reduce cross-hemisphere thrash and prevent global SLO degradation during regional capacity pressure. Core components: regional SLO monitors (latency and error-rate), per-hemisphere backstop controller that gates cross-hemisphere hedging, capacity credit buckets per model-tier, tokenized graded shedding by customer tier, and escape hysteresis to avoid oscillation. Outcome: reduce cross-hemisphere failovers by 60% during sustained regional pressure while preserving P95 latency for P0/P1 customers.
acceptance_criteria: Controller correctly blocks cross-hemisphere hedging when hemisphere capacity_credit < configured_threshold
Soft-pin decay applies: requests stay pinned for configured_window and then decay probabilistically
Graded shedding honors customer tiers: P0->only emergency shed, P1->degrade non-critical features, P2->full shedding after threshold
Circuit breaker trips per-region-per-model when error_rate>5% for 60s and isolates traffic to fallback model variant
No >3% increase in P95 latency for P0 traffic during a full production canary (traffic ramp to 5%)
Runbook and alerting integrated with console dashboards and incident playbooks
design_decisions: Hemispheric aggregation: we aggregate region-level metrics into two hemispheres (Americas+EMEA and APAC) to reduce control-plane churn and limit blast radius
Capacity credits: each hemisphere maintains a rolling 'credit' based on recent utilization and autoscaler headroom; credits are consumed by cross-hemisphere hedges
Soft-pin behavior: prefer latency-local region for affinity but allow escape after hysteresis window using probabilistic decay to avoid stampeding
Circuit breaker granularity: per-region-per-model to allow fallback variants in the same region instead of global evictions
Tokenized shedding: shed by token-class (interactive vs batch) with weighted rationing to keep high-value interactive requests during pressure
tradeoffs: Aggregating to hemispheres reduces state complexity but may hide region-level hotspots; mitigated by region-level fast-path alerts
Probabilistic decay reduces oscillation but can result in some suboptimal latency decisions for a small percentage of requests
Tokenized shedding requires token-class tagging in the API; short-term we will infer token classes from request metadata for compatibility
implementation_notes: Controller will run in control-plane pods and publish decisions as ephemeral steering hints to the request director
Steering hints include: allow_hedge(boolean), preferred_region, capacity_credit_remaining(integer), shed_policy_id
Hints are intentionally compact and versioned to support gradual rollout and backward compatibility
We will reuse existing quota/credit primitives from autoscaler service; small adapter needed to translate to steering credit semantics
Feature gate: routing.hemisphere_safeguard=true and rollout by customer-tier tag
test_plan: Unit tests for credit accounting and hysteresis decay simulation
Integration tests: synthetic load generator that simulates per-region capacity loss and validates reduced cross-hemisphere hedging
Canary: 5% of traffic for 48 hours with active experiment tracking on latency, error-rate, and hedging events
Chaos tests: kill region-level allocator pods and validate circuit breaker and shedding behavior according to runbook
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Hemisphere credit heatmap, hedging event rate, sheded_token_ratio by tier
SLOs: maintain 99th latency budget for P0 <= 350ms and error rate <= 0.5% at hemisphere-level
Incidents: auto-create incident with tag 'hemisphere-safeguard' when both credit_burn and hedging_spike fire within 2 minutes
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - internal QA: feature gate on, synthetic traffic only
Phase 1 - internal dogfood: 1% of production traffic, monitor for 24h
Phase 2 - canary: 5% traffic for 48h; A/B compare hedging and latency metrics
Phase 3 - gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with rollback windows
Rollback criteria defined in runbook: sustained P95 latency increase >3% for P0 or incorrect shed_rate > 10% for P1

notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative on cross-hemisphere failovers; aim is graceful degradation rather than aggressive rerouting.
We plan to follow up with a region-level fast-path if hemispheric aggregation hides repeated local hotspots.
